solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Possibly stymies our secret

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the two words might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a third party might be thwarting their hidden plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' is the anagram signal working on STYMIES plus OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secret is hidden or unexplained, a close synonym.

clue.text: Millions like hot potatoes

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)
as means like
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of people enjoy hot potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is the British name for mashed potatoes.

clue.text: Contemptuous racists unfortunately held up bill

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece goes within the other
unfortunately suggests the letters of the word are in a bad state, jumbled
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Bigots unfortunately delayed a piece of legislation, which shows scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' signals the anagram, 'up' turns the short word for bill in this down clue, and 'held' puts it inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sarcastic means using mocking scorn, being derisive.

clue.text: Lack of interest shown in turning up in Brunei unnecessarily

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Boredom is on display unnecessarily in the sultanate of Brunei.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden word; 'in' does that job. IUNNE, read upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is weary boredom, a listless absence of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Be disposed to wearing semi- clinging voile at the back

parts.note: if you are wearing something you are in it

indicators.note: semi- means half, so the first half of the next word
at the back picks the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone tends towards wearing a half-clingy dress of sheer voile.
explanation.definitionFit: To incline is to tend or lean towards something, to be disposed.

clue.text: State on the fringes of legality in all respects

parts.note: to utter is to say or state

indicators.note: fringes are edges, so the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Something legally borderline is described as entirely so.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly means completely, totally, in every way.

clue.text: Tough to inflict damage with only half the final number

indicators.text: with only half the final number
indicators.note: the final letter of the word for damage is the Roman numeral for 1000; half of that, 500, is a different Roman numeral which takes its place

parts.note: to harm is to inflict damage

explanation.surface: A comment on how hard it is to do much harm with only half of the last figure.
explanation.walkthrough: M, the final letter, is 1000 in Roman numerals; half of it is 500, written D. So M is swapped for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough and hard are synonyms, as in a difficult or firm thing.

clue.text: Without me foreign embassy is hell

indicators.note: without says certain letters are removed from the pool first
foreign suggests the letters are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomat finds working at an overseas embassy hellish when left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ME from EMBASSY, leaving BASSY, which 'foreign' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a bottomless pit, used as a picture of the underworld.

clue.text: I peel off after protest by left is wrecked

indicators.note: by means beside, so this piece is next to the one before
after says the following pieces come behind the earlier ones

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
to shed is to peel off, as skin

explanation.surface: Someone strips off following a protest by the left, and is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something demolished has been knocked down or destroyed.

clue.text: Lose temper about church having parsonages emptied of drink

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to snap is to lose your temper

indicators.note: emptied removes the insides of the word, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A vicar loses his temper at church because the vicarages have run out of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: It sends a warning to father by name

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Something sends a warning to a father, addressed by name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wailing device on ambulances and police cars that alerts people to danger.

clue.text: Doctor acts calmly after loss of 50 in major disaster

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters get reworked
says one letter must be taken away from the pool before rearranging

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A doctor stays calm when facing a huge catastrophe in which fifty were lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L (50 in Roman numerals) out of ACTS CALMLY, then 'Doctor' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a sudden violent upheaval, an enormous catastrophe.

clue.text: Well-known female storyteller keeps a male friend in Paris

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a liar tells stories, in the sense of fibs
ami is French for a male friend

explanation.surface: A famous woman novelist has a boyfriend in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' suggests an author, but here it means someone who tells lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something familiar is recognised easily because one has met it often.

clue.text: Known as Algerian partly through the nose

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone recognised as North African speaks with a twang through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal sound is produced with air passing through the nostrils.

clue.text: British insignia has a stripe on the edge

parts.note: an order is a decoration or badge of honour
a line is a stripe

explanation.surface: A British badge has a stripe along its border.
explanation.definitionFit: Something borderline is marginal, close to the dividing line.

clue.text: Banned newspaper ultimately responsible for gross offence

parts.note: something banned is out, as in ruled out or outlawed
a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A banned newspaper is ultimately to blame for a serious wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shocking, scandalous wrongdoing that provokes anger.

clue.text: Scary gangster providing weapons

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
arming means providing weapons

explanation.surface: A frightening mobster is supplying guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarming means frightening, causing fear or worry.

clue.text: Agreement to retain universal payment protection insurance for city careerists

indicators.note: to retain is to hold inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: yes expresses agreement
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
PPI stands for payment protection insurance, a mis-sold British loan cover

explanation.surface: A deal that keeps a loan insurance scheme for City workers.
explanation.walkthrough: PPI was a British insurance sold with loans, notorious for mis-selling claims.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word for young urban professionals, ambitious workers in finance and the City.

clue.text: Graceless in a gentle fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Something clumsy happens despite being done gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking elegance means clumsy or awkward, without grace.

clue.text: Extremely desirable to be concerned about Labour leader's state

indicators.note: extremely picks the two extreme letters of the following word
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to care is to be concerned

indicators.note: a leader is the first, so the first letter of the word before is taken

explanation.surface: It would be very good to worry about what the Labour leader says about the state of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to declare, to say something clearly and openly.

clue.text: Former monarch supports baron over independence

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman, like an earl
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An ex-king backs a nobleman against independence.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, ER 'supports' by sitting below; 'over' puts EARL above I.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means previous, preceding in time.

clue.text: Harsh south wind reaches the east

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A harsh wind from the south blows as far as the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe or stern, unforgiving and strict in manner.

clue.text: Lacking purpose on fewer occasions after taking valium regularly

indicators.note: says the following piece comes after the earlier one
regularly picks every other letter of the word

parts.note: less often means on fewer occasions

explanation.surface: Someone drifting without purpose takes valium less often.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means without direction or goal.

clue.text: Army corps to take on largely peaceful province

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so one letter of it is lost

parts.note: calm means peaceful

explanation.surface: An army unit is taking over a fairly quiet region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' here drops the first letter of CALM rather than the last, which is a loose use.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field, so it can mean a province or sphere.

clue.text: A tie of course

definitions.meaning: a cravat-style neckcloth worn by men
a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A draw, of course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a broad neck scarf and a famous royal racecourse.

clue.text: Fits of anger over a politician lead to riots

indicators.note: over means covering, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: rages are fits of anger
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Angry outbursts aimed at a politician end in civil unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush around violently, a close synonym for running riot.

clue.text: Change in legal terminology

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A shift in legal jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to modify, to make different.

clue.text: Reportedly capture places such as Canterbury and York

definitions.text: places such as Canterbury and York

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word as heard, not as written

parts.note: to seize is to capture

explanation.surface: Reports say there were captures at Canterbury and York.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's seat; Canterbury and York are the two archbishoprics.

clue.text: Motivation to evict nine after redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment suggests the letters are rebuilt into a new form

explanation.surface: A developer is motivated to throw out nine tenants after a building project.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is something that spurs one on, a reason or motivating factor.

clue.text: Discover the origins of truly remarkable expert

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the first letters of the next words

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Someone finds out where a really outstanding specialist came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track it down and find it.

clue.text: Consumes pheasant and pork for example without the head

indicators.note: says the leading letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pheasant and pork are examples of meats

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into game and pork, leaving out the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food is to consume it.

clue.text: Farah initially deteriorates without speed from blocks

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word before it
without means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: rusts means corrodes, deteriorates
rate means speed

explanation.surface: The runner Mo Farah starts poorly, lacking pace out of the starting blocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside. Mo Farah is a British long-distance runner.
explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate a plan is to thwart or obstruct it, as blocks does.
